title: That's my Egg! early access starts 1 January
summary: Steal an egg, outrun its guardian and see what hatches. Early access begins on Roblox at 9 am AEST (Brisbane) on Friday 1 January 2027.
imageAlt: Illustration of Labraduck chasing a player running away with an egg

sections.heading: Steal an egg. Then run.
paragraphs: Your first egg run takes you into Sunnyside Backyard, where a Labrador crossed with a duck watches over the nests. The plan is simple. Grab an egg, get it back to Home and hatch it to find out what you've added to your creature collection.
Labraduck takes egg theft personally.
sections.imageAlt: Labraduck standing on the grass in Sunnyside Backyard
sections.imageCaption: Labraduck in Sunnyside Backyard. Studio development screenshot, 7 November 2026.

sections.heading: A fresh start
paragraphs: All player progress resets when early access opens. We're still building the game, and we'll keep sharing what changes along the way.
Roblox age and account requirements apply.

title: Welcome to That's my Egg!
summary: Steal an egg, make it Home, and see what hatches. Meet the game we're building at Orchard Studios.
imageAlt: The current Labraduck guardian standing on the grass in Sunnyside Backyard
imageCaption: Labraduck in Sunnyside Backyard. Studio development capture, 7 November 2026.

sections.heading: The eggs belong to someone
paragraphs: That's my Egg! is a Roblox game about stealing eggs from guardians and getting them back to Home. The guardians have rather strong opinions about this.
Make it back with an egg, hatch it, and add the creature inside to your collection. Build up your garden and choose a pet to take along on the next run.

sections.heading: Further from Home
paragraphs: Your first trip takes you into Sunnyside Backyard. Further out are farms, woodland, reefs, an island, and mountain and sky regions still being developed.
Each region has its own creatures to discover. Some pets can be ridden; others help while following you. A useful companion is a good idea when your main plan is to run away.
sections.imageAlt: Hamsturtle on the current path beside Ripplewater Lake
sections.imageCaption: Hamsturtle at Ripplewater Lake. Studio development capture, 7 November 2026.

sections.heading: Follow the build
paragraphs: We'll post a development update every four days, with new creatures, changes to the world, and a look at what we're working on. The wiki has creature profiles and guides if you'd like a closer look.
Want to help test it? Join the early playtester list with your Roblox username, then look out for a friend request from OrchardStudios.
Early access begins on Friday 1 January 2027 at 9 am AEST (Brisbane). All player progress resets when early access opens. Until then, Roblox access may be limited while we test the game.
sections.imageAlt: The current Porcupython guardian on the path through Acorn Woods
sections.imageCaption: Porcupython in Acorn Woods. Studio development capture, 7 November 2026.

title: The guardians got bigger. You didn't.
summary: New companions to help with the getaway, bigger guardians to get away from, and a better-looking world to run through. Here's what changed over 6 to 7 November.
imageAlt: The current Donkeyote creature model, with tall ears, a golden mane, and a bushy tail
imageCaption: Donkeyote, photographed from the current game model in Studio on 7 November 2026.

sections.heading: A few new faces
paragraphs: Donkeyote, Goosemoose, Kiwink, and Fennthorn have moved from artwork into the development build, with their eggs and animations. There are now a few more reasons to take an egg that isn't yours.
Donkeyote also brings Endurance when following you, helping your running stamina last longer. Handy company for a game in which a large part of the plan involves leaving.

sections.heading: Antlers at the lake
paragraphs: Goosemoose belongs at Ripplewater Lake. Broad wings, a long neck, and a substantial set of antlers make it fairly easy to spot.
As a following pet, Goosemoose brings Tide rider to help you swim faster. If your route home involves water, that's a useful friend to have along.
sections.imageAlt: The current Goosemoose model with broad wings, a long neck, and branching antlers
sections.imageCaption: Goosemoose's current game model. Studio development photo, 7 November 2026.

sections.heading: A little help getting away
paragraphs: Kiwink joins the creatures of Acorn Woods. Its long bill is good for nosing through leaf litter; its Fleet foot benefit helps you run faster while it follows you.
You can only take one active companion at a time, so choose between help with stamina, swimming, running, or another pet's benefit before heading out. Looking adorable is a bonus.
sections.imageAlt: The current brown Kiwink model with a long bill, small wings, and a scaled tail
sections.imageCaption: Kiwink's current game model. Studio development photo, 7 November 2026.

sections.heading: About those guardians
paragraphs: All 14 biome guardians are now 25% bigger. Labraduck, Mooroo, Dandylion, and Dragorilla have refreshed models as well.
The eggs haven't got any less tempting. The thing watching them has simply become harder to ignore.

sections.heading: Nicer scenery for your escape
paragraphs: Acorn Woods has new leaf and bark textures across its trees, and we fixed a small gap at the tip of the pine. Do try to appreciate the woodland while sprinting through it.
The Jungle's ocean entrance has more connected sand and water along the coast. A little space has moved from Forest to Jungle, too, without making the overall journey longer.
Over at Lost World, a partly buried Triceratops skeleton now marks the beach landing. It's scenery. If it starts chasing you, something has gone very wrong.

sections.heading: Know what you are hatching
paragraphs: Creature information now includes a separate Animal combination field, so you can see the two animals behind each design alongside the species description.
These are changes to our development build. Gameplay testing and polish are still ahead.

title: You've got mail. Some of it hatches.
summary: Leave eggs for friends at Home, spot waiting deliveries at a glance, and meet two new faces in the Golden Dunes development build.
imageAlt: An egg-shaped teal mailbox with a small envelope and waiting-mail count above it
imageCaption: The Home mailbox and its waiting-mail badge. Studio preview with sample counts.

sections.heading: A parcel that might hatch
paragraphs: In the development build, you can put eggs and items in another player's mailbox.

When something arrives, only the owner sees the envelope and count above their mailbox. Open it to collect the delivery into Inventory. If you were only stopping by to admire the place, the red heart lets you leave a weekly like. Tap it again if you've had second thoughts.

sections.heading: A bright beak in Golden Dunes
paragraphs: Camoucan and Swobra now have eggs in the Golden Dunes development build. Camoucan has long legs, dark wings and a bright orange beak that's doing a poor job of blending in.
sections.imageAlt: Camoucan with long tan legs, dark wings and a large orange beak
sections.imageCaption: Camoucan's current game model, photographed in Studio.

sections.heading: And a very different silhouette
paragraphs: Swobra has pale feathers, a long tail and a gold marking on its flared neck. Those are two more creatures to look out for when you're deciding which egg is worth the run home.

We tested two players sending and collecting a pair of eggs in Studio. We also checked the new Golden Dunes eggs and hatch models in Studio Edit; those encounters still need gameplay testing. Everything here is a development preview.
sections.imageAlt: Swobra with pale feathers, a long tail and a gold marking on its flared neck
sections.imageCaption: Swobra's current game model, photographed in Studio.

title: The sky went dark. Then came the egg.
summary: A rare eclipse brings a meteor to Sunnyside Backyard. Crack it before dusk for a chance to bring home an egg, and take a look at the new cliffs on the way.
imageAlt: A dark eclipse disc with a pale halo above blue clouds
imageCaption: The eclipse effect in a Studio preview.

sections.heading: Something fell near the gate
paragraphs: In the development build, a rare eclipse sends a meteor down just beyond the Home gate in Sunnyside Backyard. Once it lands, you can crack it with a club or an empty hand. Hits from different players count toward breaking the same rock.

The meteor drops one or two eggs. Pick one up before dusk and bring it to your garden to hatch a Grim Creeper. As a follower, it reduces fall damage. A considerate feature for something that arrived by falling out of the sky.
sections.imageAlt: A dark meteor rock, a purple egg with glowing blue veins, and the blocky purple Grim Creeper
sections.imageCaption: The meteor, egg and Grim Creeper beside one another in Studio.

sections.heading: A new look on the way to Clover Farm
paragraphs: Three tiers of grassy cliffs now run from Home through Sunnyside Backyard and Clover Farm. The Backyard fences match the cream pickets at the Home gate, down to the little eggs on the posts.
sections.imageAlt: Cream picket fencing with egg-shaped finials in front of three grassy cliff tiers
sections.imageCaption: The Backyard fences and cliffs in the development build.

sections.heading: What we've checked
paragraphs: We've checked the meteor assets, hatch model and new scenery in Studio. The full eclipse encounter and the updated route still need gameplay testing.

title: Dinner first. Egg theft second.
summary: A meal can buy you a quiet moment at the nest. We've also given wild eggs woven nests and added a little more life around Ripplewater Lake.
imageAlt: Two patterned eggs resting in a straw bowl with a woven wooden rim in Clover Farm
imageCaption: New woven nests in Clover Farm. Studio Edit preview, 18 November.

sections.heading: Twenty seconds of peace
paragraphs: In the development build, giving suitable food to a calm wild parent keeps it busy eating for 20 seconds. You can take an egg of its species during that meal without starting a chase from that parent.
An unfed partner can still come after you. Bring enough for both. Apparently stealing the children is acceptable, provided you've catered.
Once the meal ends, normal aggression returns. Food won't calm a parent that's already angry, so dinner needs to come before the incident.

sections.heading: Better accommodation for eggs
paragraphs: All 42 wild nests now have woven rims and straw bowls shaped into the ground. From Clover Farm to Lost World, the eggs have somewhere to sit that looks like someone meant to put them there.
Even the underwater nests have shallower bowls fitted to the seabed. Considerable effort has gone into housing the eggs you intend to remove.
sections.imageAlt: Two large turquoise patterned eggs in a woven nest surrounded by tall grass in Lost World
sections.imageCaption: Lost World's eggs in their new nest. Studio Edit preview, 18 November.

sections.heading: A moment by the lake
paragraphs: Ripplewater Lake has flowering lily pads, cattails and rocks along its shore, plus a short wooden side pier and a blue-and-cream tackle nook.
The nook is scenery for now. No shopkeeper is waiting to sell you an emergency excuse.
sections.imageAlt: A small covered wooden pier beside lily pads and cattails along Ripplewater Lake
sections.imageCaption: The new lake shoreline and covered pier. Studio Edit preview, 19 November.

sections.heading: Still in development
paragraphs: These changes have been checked in Studio Edit. Feeding encounters, egg pickups, dawn spawning and movement around the new scenery still need gameplay testing. The photos show the development build, including unfinished surroundings.

title: The meteor brought company.
summary: Seven possible meteor hatches, three new Moonbeam creatures, and a sandstone welcome in Golden Dunes. Your creature collection has a few more gaps to fill.
imageAlt: Noddlepod's spotted pink body, curled antennae and blue face in a staged Studio portrait
imageCaption: Noddlepod, photographed from its installed game model in Studio on 22 November.

sections.heading: Seven possible passengers
paragraphs: Meteor eggs have more surprises inside. In the development build, an egg from Meteore can now hatch Grim Creeper, Noddlepod, Hushstilt, Orbwink, Riftshell, Cindergoo or Starfrill. Each species has the same chance.
That gives Grim Creeper six new neighbours in the meteor collection. Noddlepod has curled antennae and a spotted coat. Orbwink appears to have spent most of its budget on eyes.
sections.imageAlt: The pale Orbwink creature with enormous glossy black eyes, blue markings and small hands
sections.imageCaption: Orbwink's current game model. Staged Studio portrait, 22 November.

sections.heading: Further from home
paragraphs: Moonbeam Expanse has three more creatures to discover: Lumifin, Sneezepuff and Skitterhusk. Their eggs are in the area's normal daily pool in the development build.
Lumifin has four soft fins, Sneezepuff has a fluffy coat and plume tail, and Skitterhusk has broad fin-paws. The naming department has been left unsupervised again.

sections.heading: A grand entrance in Golden Dunes
paragraphs: Sandstone cliffs now frame the route through Golden Dunes, with Meerkabou Sentinels set into the canyon walls.
One is pictured below, holding an egg in an elaborate gold-and-turquoise shrine. A very expensive way of saying 'please don't touch that'.
sections.imageAlt: A Meerkabou sentinel holding an egg in a gold and turquoise sandstone shrine between canyon cliffs
sections.imageCaption: A Meerkabou sentinel in the new Golden Dunes canyon. Studio Edit preview, 22 November.

sections.heading: What we've checked
paragraphs: We've checked the new hatches and Moonbeam's daily egg changes in Studio. Collecting an egg from the full meteor encounter and travelling through the new desert route still need testing.
These are development previews. The alien portraits were staged in Studio, and the surrounding world is still being built.
